Hey there Dexx4d. So right now I am really focus on the content side and am mostly working out the workflow for generating 360 degree videos and how to tell stories with this technology from a film making point of view.

I am using 3d studio with mental ray renderer to generate imagery right now, but also have been doing panos with a 3 camera DSLR rig to get a feel for shooting live action in 360 (opr in this case 180x180).

Its a huge difference trying to tell a story in 3d vers 2d. All the old traditional film making techniques are moot now within the 3d space. Everything from how to rig the shot and how to setup cameras and lighting and microphones and hide the crew (all can be seen now in 3d) to how to carry a story and lead the viewer in 3d without braking the immersion. It's all new terriroty indeed and don't get me started on figuring out the backend editing. (I use permier cs 6 for editing BTW)

Soon I hope somebody will develop a 360 movie player that will allow hotlinking an area of the film to another one (so you could hotlink a door or window in your current, that a end vieiwer could click on and then go down the hall to another room out climb out the window)

other then that I use carboard and am going down the samsung VR road I think.

A HUGE problem I am finding is fragmentation across the mediums. No two headset display content the same way, so as a developer you have to develop for many different units and package for different technologies to be able to get across the mass spectrum of devices and there are no good marketplaces yet to sell content too. Both issues I suspect will be solved inthe next year or so...

I've been working as a developer, mostly in Unity, for about five years now. I've worked mostly on games, including a museum installation to teach kids about space, but also a business app and training simulation. I think VR is a great platform for immersive interactive fiction. Have you considered going the interactive story/experience direction, instead of just an on-rails 3D experience/recording?

Oh yes. In fact most of my ideas have a interactive element to them. I'm really interested in non-linear storytelling and /or telling the same story, but from different points of view in real time. What I'm doing with the 360 stuff is getting hands on experience with the current technologies and developing workflows through trial and error mostly. Seeing how the tools sets work, what the weaknesses and strengths are, that sort of thing...

I love unity and have played around myself, but at its hart its a game engine. I'm looking to make more photo realistic experience and since I am a film maker, I am interested in using film making tools to do it.

I fully believe however that in just a few short years the tools like unity will be much more graphically realistic and /or the film tools (adobe permier or aftereffects) will be able to support interactivity.

In fact I'm hoping that soon the vr video players will start supporting "hotspots' similar to how current web based 360 panos can be hot linked. Once that happens we can start making interactive "choose your own adventure" type stories with 360 film. I bet we get that technology in just a matter of months... Seems easy-ish to implement
